annotations.text: Habit won a six-way build. The finding that outlived the five alternatives: all of them independently chose a COMPOSITE preview over active-tab-only, and the literal spec build showed why — read literally each tab owns its own calendar, so a coach cannot see a Monday collision until validation rejects it.

The client booking flow, end to end, in the Forest theme.

The three-month window on step 1 is a UI restriction only — nothing validates against it server-side, which is what lets a recurring booking run past it.

CHOSEN: Timeline, the measured strip. Width IS duration — a 60-minute lesson occupies twice the space of a 30-minute one, and the two-hour midday gap is real empty space rather than a label.

Open problem carried forward: that squeezes the 30-minute slots narrow enough that their labels rotate 90°. Needs a rethink at phone width, not a reflow.

The student picker in the header is not in the spec — added because price resolves from the student's override before the block price, so the page cannot render a price until it knows who the lesson is for.
Partial success is the normal case, not an error state. The reason is deliberately merged — saying \"already taken\" would leak that another family holds that slot.

Client sign-up, built from the data model and ADR-002 as summarised there (no separate sign-up doc was found). Fields map to the Client record: clientName, clientEmail, clientPhone, clientRelationship (SELF | PARENT | GUARDIAN), smsOptIn. Each skater becomes a Student with isMinor and studentStatus = PENDING, plus a CLIENT# → STUDENT# link.

Auth is Cognito, on custom pages (ASSUMED — not Managed Login).

Empty state: nothing typed yet. Continue stays disabled until a code resolves to a coach, and the placeholder card shows where the coach's name will appear so families can check it's the right person before creating an account.

ASSUMED: the coach-code format. 'DANA-7K2Q' is a placeholder — ADR-002 leaves length, character set and expiry open. The code resolves through CODE#<coachCode> (access pattern 9) before any account exists, so the page can show the coach's name on step 1. It is held client-side until step 4, when the skaters are linked to that coach.

COGNITO: 'Create account' calls SignUp. Email is the username; name and phone go as standard attributes. The password checklist mirrors Cognito's default policy (8+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol) — if the pool's policy changes, this list must change with it.

COGNITO: ConfirmSignUp with the emailed code (Cognito's default is a 6-digit code, valid 24 h). On success the app signs in, and only then is anything written to DynamoDB — the CLIENT# profile and, on the next step, the students. Resend = ResendConfirmationCode.

Variant of step 4 when 'Who are the lessons for?' = Me (clientRelationship = SELF). The client IS the student: one Student row with studentName = clientName, isMinor = false, studentStatus = PENDING. No add-another-skater here. ASSUMED: a SELF client books only for themselves, and a minor can't sign up as SELF. Whether one person can be SELF and also a PARENT isn't decided — clientRelationship lives on the Client record, so today it's one or the other.
No Back button from here on: the Cognito account already exists and is confirmed, so going 'back' would mean editing the profile, not undoing a step.

A PENDING student cannot book (ADR-002 d2), so the result screen is a waiting state, not a booking prompt. The email is already verified by step 3, so this screen no longer asks the family to check their inbox. ASSUMED: no cap on skaters per client — ADR-016 notes the session policy is comfortable at 1–4.

Coach sign-up, from ADR-017 and the Coach record in the data model. How a coach account comes to exist is still OPEN (ADR-002 / ADR-016) — this design assumes self-serve Cognito sign-up on custom pages, which ADR-016 flags as letting anyone start collecting children's data. Treat it as a proposal until that is decided. If coaches are admin-invited instead (AdminCreateUser), steps 1–2 become 'set your password' from an invite email.
COGNITO: 'Create account' calls SignUp — the account exists from this click. Login email is the Cognito username (the Coach record's `email`). Password checklist mirrors Cognito's default policy.

COGNITO: ConfirmSignUp with the 6-digit code. This verifies the LOGIN email only. It does not satisfy ADR-017 d5 — Cognito's verification of the login address does not establish that the coach wants that address in front of families — so the business email still gets its own link on step 4. The two are deliberately worded as code vs link.

Signed in by now. 'Save and continue' writes COACH#<coachId> / PROFILE in DynamoDB (not Cognito attributes), generates the coach code, and sends the ADR-017 confirmation link. ADR-017 d4: businessEmail is required, pre-filled with the login email, editable, with the ADR's help text. Also: coachTz, currency, lateCancellationHours, paymentInstructions. ASSUMED: 24 h default notice.

DIFFERENT-EMAIL BRANCH. ADR-017 d5/d7: the business-email link is BladeBook's own flow (token, expiry, route) — Cognito doesn't provide it. No schedule can be written until businessEmailVerifiedAt exists, hence the locked 'Build your teaching week' card. 'Use my login email instead' switches to the same-email branch without waiting for the link.

AFTER SIGN-UP (ADR-017 d5b–d5d). Listed = verified: the list is exactly the login email plus unexpired verifiedEmails entries, built server-side. Picking a listed address saves instantly — no link, no hold. '+ Use a new address' is the only path to a link. Remove appears on every row except the current business email (switch first) and the login email (verified by Cognito on every request); removing deletes the entry, so the address stops being listed and would need a link again. Expiry (365 days after an address stops being used, d5c) just makes the row disappear — no dates shown. The header text is decision 4's required Reply-To explanation, not verification help.

SAME-EMAIL BRANCH (ADR-017 d5a, owner 2026-09-24). When businessEmail equals the coach's Cognito-verified login email, no link is sent: the profile write sets businessEmailVerifiedAt in the same PutItem, step 4 is skipped, and the teaching week is unlocked immediately. The comparison is server-side against the signed-in token's email claim with email_verified = true — never against a value the form sends — trimmed and case-insensitive.

Added 2026-09-30 from the current ADRs: two dashboard buttons and the time-off form (ADR-008 d6a, d6b), the overlap rejection (ADR-008 d8), the review step with re-pricing and the must-tick large-price warning (ADR-020; the 50% shown is a demo value — the real threshold is undecided), and the status after saving (ADR-010 d5l). The clickable version is the BladeBook Schedule Builder prototype.

Added 2026-09-30. Week view and cancel preview: ADR-009 d5, d5a, d7 — 'this week' is the Sun–Sat week on screen from now on, release-or-hold is asked per lesson. Payments: ADR-003, ADR-015 d4 (a no-show shows its full price for now). Lesson list: ADR-014 d8. Profile switches and the coach cancellation text: ADR-016 d7a, ADR-009 d9.

Added 2026-09-30. Cancel confirmation wording: ADR-009 d2 (MVP 'may incur'). Recurrence management: ADR-009 d4, d4a, d4b, ADR-015 d1a. Result after a failed attempt: ADR-006 d4b (booked / already booked for this student / unavailable, and the keep-or-cancel prompt). Empty calendar: ADR-008.

Added 2026-09-30, phone-sized. ADR-014: offline queue and banner (d1, d1a), cancelling disabled offline (ADR-009 d5a), today’s lessons not loaded (d5a), contacts only with signal (d9b), cancel confirmation with the confirm button away from the first tap (ADR-009 d5a), rejected check-ins (d4a), family cancelled after a replay (d4).
